answer: Sybil resistance is enforced at admission: every new identity must mine a one-time proof-of-work, finding a nonce whose SHA-256 digest starts with a required run of leading zero bits. The work is real CPU time and electricity paid per account, and difficulty rises with load, so a farm of fakes pays per head. Even if an attacker wants one puppet called summit to dominate, the extra aliases cedar and dune each need their own burned proof before they count. Influence thus costs compute per identity, which is what stops mass registration.
